_comment: Week-1 research pass, gathered 2026-08-21. Sources named per field. FRED and every market-data host are blocked from this environment's egress proxy, so the FRED-series values below were web-sourced into fred_fallback rather than pulled from the API; once FRED_API_KEY is set in a routine that can reach api.stlouisfed.org, the live series take precedence automatically.

spx_current.source: S&P 500 close 2026-08-20 (TheStreet / vittarthi market wraps; CNBC quotes 7,723.55 at the 08-19 close)

cape_web.source: web consensus 2026-08-20: thetrading.tools 41.2, gurufocus 41.4 (Aug 1), multpl 41.8, chartrow 40.4 - multpl.com is blocked from this environment so the mid-range print is used

buffett_indicator.source: buffettindicator.org / thetrading.tools, 2026-08-20. currentmarketvaluation.com prints ~291% on a Q2-2026 annualised-GDP denominator; both are far past the 200% top-of-range anchor

fiscal.source: CBO Budget and Economic Outlook 2026-2036: FY2026 deficit $1.9tn = 5.8% of GDP. Debt/GDP 122.6% (Q1 2026, FRED GFDEGDQ188S via govspending); gross debt passed $40tn on 2026-08-18 per CRFB

cpi_fallback.source: BLS CPI release 2026-08-12: headline +3.4% y/y in July 2026 (down from 3.5% in June); core 2.5%

fred_fallback.source: 10y 4.65% and 2y 4.19% on 2026-08-20 (10y touched a 20-month high of 4.75% earlier that week); ICE BofA HY OAS 2.70% on 2026-08-17, 2.71% average for August

_curve_note: The 2s10s un-inverted on 2024-09-05, which is inside the trailing 36 months, so FRAMEWORK 1.7's post-inversion asterisk applies: +46bps scores 3.0, and the 12-18 month post-un-inversion window closed around March 2026.

fed.stance: hold 3.50-3.75% (9-3 vote, 28-29 July), three dissents wanting a HIKE, September hike priced near 61%
fed.read: policy headwind, and the bias is toward tightening, not easing - Warsh has been chair since 2026-05-13 and delivers his debut Jackson Hole speech in late August

statement.summary: Raised S&P 500 target to 8,400 on 'fabulous earnings momentum' - now among the Street's highest

sentiment_updates.name: Wood
sentiment_updates.note: 'Golden Age' thesis intact: deflationary tech + fiscal push

statement.summary: Q2-26 13F: book up to $15.4bn across 191 names; Tesla/AMD/SpaceX/Tempus/Robinhood ~25% of assets

sentiment_updates.name: Lee
sentiment_updates.note: 8,000 near-term target BUT explicitly warns of bear-market-like moves Aug-Oct

statement.summary: S&P to 7,900-8,000 this month ('the bigger the base, the bigger the breakout'), year-end 8,000+ with upside to 8,400-8,800 - while flagging four H2 triggers

sentiment_updates.name: Siegel
sentiment_updates.note: constructive but names AI spend, valuations and bond yields as the worries

statement.summary: Weak July payrolls 'overstate' labour-market weakness; still does not expect a bear market

sentiment_updates.name: Sonders
sentiment_updates.note: 36m cut to 0: record margin debt, record equity allocations and index concentration are her stated longer-term risks

statement.summary: Rotation backdrop persists and higher yields are biting; investors are 'reluctantly' long via ETF flows and margin debt

sentiment_updates.name: Druckenmiller
sentiment_updates.note: REVEALED PREFERENCE: talks little, deployed hard - upgraded on positioning, not rhetoric

statement.summary: Q2-26 13F: book +54% q/q to $5.21bn, 48 new positions; exited Broadcom/Intel/Micron entirely, raised Amazon >1,000% - a semis-to-megacap rotation, not a de-risking

sentiment_updates.name: Roubini
sentiment_updates.note: baseline still 'Goldilocks', but names a more fragile backdrop: Middle East war, AI job-shedding, private-credit stress

statement.summary: Holds the Goldilocks 2026 baseline - tariffs walked back, growth slower, inflation only modestly higher

sentiment_updates.name: Slok
sentiment_updates.note: 24m cut to -1: AI capex is running at ~0.85pp of GDP/yr vs 0.5pp in the housing boom, and he warns it 'can unwind at a similar pace'. Bull economy / bear market, with the risk framing moving from stagflation to overheating

statement.summary: AI capex growing nearly twice as fast as the housing boom; rising consumer delinquencies and a widening K-shaped economy on the other side of the ledger

sentiment_updates.name: El-Erian
sentiment_updates.note: 24m cut to -1 and conviction up: long-rate/fiscal risk is now his central case, not a side worry

statement.summary: Calls Treasury's doubled bond buybacks a short-term fix - 'financial engineering' that leaves the debt and deficit causes of surging long rates untouched

sentiment_updates.name: Gross
sentiment_updates.note: 'No crash, just a forward weave requiring a cane'; bearish long Treasuries on deficits, prefers energy infrastructure and MLPs to exuberant tech

statement.summary: Valuation casts a shadow over 2026; the record rally is at risk of stalling unless AI earnings show up

sentiment_updates.name: Buffett-Berkshire
sentiment_updates.note: REVEALED PREFERENCE FLIPPED: first net buying in 15 quarters. Cash still $365bn, so the caution is real - but the direction of travel reversed

statement.summary: Q2-26: ~$19.8bn net equity purchases after 14 straight quarters of net selling; cash $397.4bn -> $365.5bn; $4.5bn of buybacks; Alphabet now the third-largest holding at $36.6bn

sentiment_updates.name: Marks
sentiment_updates.note: current worry is private credit, not public equity: fast capital deployment into direct lending, with PE portfolio-company performance as the hinge

statement.summary: Memo 'What's Going On in Private Credit?' - direct lending's growth, and the issues rapid deployment created

sentiment_updates.name: Dimon
sentiment_updates.note: 12m cut to -3, but the rhetoric>action gap stands: JPM keeps lending and underwriting while he says he would not buy

statement.summary: 'Margin debt is the highest it has ever been', much of it hidden in prime brokerage, ETFs and Treasury-basis trades; says he would not buy the S&P 500 or long-dated Treasuries at today's prices and the market is one bad trade from panic selling

sentiment_updates.name: Krugman
sentiment_updates.note: bearish the real economy rather than the index - the gap between the two is his point

statement.summary: August Substack run - 'An Explosion of Misery' (Aug 5) and 'This is your economy on crack (spread)' (Aug 13): the US economy is in worse shape than the tape looks

sentiment_updates.name: Dalio
sentiment_updates.note: conviction up: says his own indicators already put AI stocks in bubble territory, and the next crisis is sovereign rather than banking

statement.summary: Late-stage debt cycle; Fed balance-sheet expansion is 'stimulus into a bubble'; most likely path is a 1970s-style stagflationary spiral with the Fed monetising

sentiment_updates.name: Rosenberg
sentiment_updates.note: conviction up: says credit markets are already writing the warning - directly relevant to the HY tripwire

statement.summary: With Richard Bernstein: the AI trade is a bubble, real disposable income is fractionally negative y/y, and ex-AI the four-quarter real GDP trend is under 1.5% - a K-shaped economy where profits take all the income growth

sentiment_updates.name: Grantham
sentiment_updates.note: latest sourced statement is June 2026 - inside the 6-month window but not fresh this fortnight

statement.summary: Calls this 'the most expensive market in American history'; a reversion to trend would be closer to a wipeout than a correction, and the odds an AI bubble does not bust are 'slim to none'

sentiment_updates.name: Burry
sentiment_updates.note: Scion stopped filing 13Fs in Nov 2025 - positions now come from his Cassandra Unchained Substack, so the disclosure lag is his choice and the newest trades (Aug 4) are paywalled

statement.summary: Disclosed bearish book: puts on NVDA and PLTR at up to ~80% of the portfolio (~$1.1bn notional), plus TSLA, CAT, AMAT, SMH and MU opened 30 June and added 24 July

reading_list.title: Consumer Price Index Summary — July 2026
reading_list.why: 3.4% headline / 2.5% core is the inflation leg of the Excess CAPE Yield calculation and the reason the Fed's dot plot still leans hike.

reading_list.title: Chair Warsh's FOMC press conference transcript, 29 July 2026
reading_list.why: The 9-3 hold with three dissents wanting a hike is the policy headwind in my Fed block - read the dissent language before his Jackson Hole debut.

reading_list.title: Q&A: Gross Debt Versus Debt Held by the Public
reading_list.why: Gross debt passed $40tn on 18 August. This is the denominator question behind my fiscal tile - 122.6% gross vs ~100% held-by-public changes what the 4.5 score means.

reading_list.title: Berkshire Hathaway Turns Buyer As Buffett Backs Alphabet
reading_list.why: The single biggest revealed-preference change on my roster: ~$19.8bn of net buying after 14 straight quarters of selling, with cash still at $365bn.

reading_list.title: When Everybody Is on the Same Side of the Trade — Rosenberg & Bernstein
reading_list.why: Their claim that credit markets are already flashing the warning is a direct test of my HY-spread tripwire, which is still pinned at 270bps.
